title: Food From Many Cultures
strapline: Rice and dumplings, flatbread and plantain — a taste of the whole world.
intent: Sharing foods from many cultures helps children see the richness of the world and value ways of eating different from their own.
Tasting, cooking and naming foods from around the world builds vocabulary, curiosity and real knowledge.
Preparing food together — mixing, rolling, serving — is rich sensory and physical play with a purpose.
Inviting families to share a dish or a food tradition honours every child's heritage and builds community.
The theme opens gentle talk about how different families eat, celebrate and share meals.
implementation: Offer a role-play kitchen or tasting table with foods and utensils from a range of cultures — chopsticks, tortillas, rice, spices to smell.
Invite families to share a favourite dish, ingredient or mealtime tradition, and celebrate each one.
Cook something together — flatbread, dumplings, a fruit from far away — talking about where it comes from.
Feed in vocabulary and knowledge lightly: names of foods, how they're eaten, which country they come from.
Keep the talk warm and respectful — 'In lots of families people eat with their hands, or with chopsticks' — no food is strange.
Follow the children — some will cook and serve, others will taste and name and sort.
key_questions: What does your family like to eat together?
Have you tasted this before — what does it remind you of?
How is this food eaten — with a fork, chopsticks, or hands?
Where in the world does this food come from?
What smells and colours can you notice on the table?

impact.text: Children taste and name foods from different cultures and build food vocabulary.
Children talk about their own family's food and notice other families eat differently.
Children help prepare and serve food, using tools and their hands with care.
Children show respect and curiosity for ways of eating unlike their own.
Children explore new tastes, smells and textures with open curiosity.

enhancements: A world-foods tasting table (allergy-checked) with foods families have shared.
A multicultural role-play kitchen with woks, tortilla presses, chopsticks and rice bowls.
A cooking session making a dish from one child's family tradition.
A spice-and-smell station — cinnamon, cardamom, ginger — to explore with noses.
A 'foods we love' display with family photos and drawings of favourite meals.

playing_exploring: Children taste, smell and handle foods from many places with open curiosity.
They cook and serve in a kitchen rich with cultures.
active_learning: Children see a cooking task through from mixing to serving.
They try new tastes and textures, willing to have a go.
creating_thinking: Children connect foods to families, places and their own experience.
They notice similarities and differences in how people eat.
